sources.entry: Theia | Cloud & desktop IDE framework implemented in TypeScript

summary.one_liner: Eclipse Theia is an extensible framework for building full-fledged, multi-language Cloud and Desktop IDEs and tools using web technologies.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Theia as a framework for building browser-based and desktop IDEs and tools. It is built to be highly flexible so adopters can assemble their own IDE. It supports the VS Code extension protocol, so VS Code-style extensions can run in Theia. The README links to guides for building a Theia application, writing Theia extensions, writing VS Code-like extensions, testing VS Code extensions in Theia, and packaging a desktop app with Electron. It also links to API docs, a VS Code API compatibility report, and coding guidelines. Releases are published on GitHub with changelogs, and each release now includes a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM).
use_cases: create a desktop IDE with Electron
run VS Code extensions in a custom editor
embed an IDE-style tool in a web app
contribute to an open-source IDE framework
how_to_run: See the README's Getting Started links on the Theia website for setup guides
Fork the repository and run the examples from source (per README Contributing section)
notable: Supports the VS Code extension protocol
Builds both browser-based and desktop IDEs from one framework
Vendor-neutral open-source governance under the Eclipse Foundation
Publishes an SBOM for every release to the Eclipse Foundation SBOM registry
Includes a VS Code API compatibility report
caveats: The README does not include install commands; setup details are on the external Theia website
